applied.problem: "So torque = I × α" read alone on a card says the motor torque sets α, but only the net torque does once a load or friction acts; the bold line and practice already say net torque.

Absolute claims fail: variable capacitors exist, and pulling the plates of an isolated charged capacitor apart lowers C and raises V with no current, the same kind of change as pulling a mass inward; also the spin-up needs no outside torque, not none at all.
